points.description: States that linked lists can be of variable length / size, i.e. they can grow or shrink dynamically (no fixed size as in arrays). Equivalent wording such as 'dynamic size' or 'not fixed in size' is accepted.
points.partial_credit: 2-3 marks for a vague or related statement, e.g. easy insertion/deletion or flexible memory use, without saying size can vary; or the idea stated with a minor error.

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for stating that a linked list's length is variable/dynamic, can grow or shrink, in any wording, even very briefly. Part marks (2-3) for related but incomplete advantages such as easy insertion/deletion or not needing contiguous memory, or for the fact mixed with a minor error. No marks for unrelated or incorrect claims, such as faster random access. Extra correct detail is fine.
